title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Obj. 1: If the death is a sufficient ransom, all must already be restored
pass_a_gloss: Christ's death was either a sufficient ransom (λυτρον) for wiping out (dispungenda) the sins of the human race, and for placing all humans back into the state of grace and reconciliation, or insufficient. If it is stated insufficient, we diminish (extenuamus) Divine grace, and we trample undeservedly on Christ's merit. If it is acknowledged sufficient, then with a sufficient cause placed in act, nothing else is required for inducing the effect. From the very act therefore of Christ offering himself to God there would follow at once universal liberation of all humans from the guilt (reatu) of their sins, and universal reconciliation, or reception of all humans into Divine grace.
pass_b_english: Either Christ's death was a sufficient ransom to wipe away the sins of the human race and put every human being back into grace and reconciliation, or it was insufficient. Call it insufficient, and we diminish divine grace and trample Christ's merit. Grant that it was sufficient, and then—once that sufficient cause has been put into act—nothing else is required to bring about the effect. From Christ's very act of offering himself to God, therefore, there would follow at once the universal liberation of all people from the guilt of their sins, and a universal reconciliation: that is, the reception of everyone into divine grace.
source_text: Christi mors aut sufficiens fuit λυτρον ad dispungenda peccata humani generis, omnesque homines in statum gratiae & reconciliationis reponendos, aut insufficiens. Si statuatur insufficiens, gratiam Divinam extenuamus, & meritum Christi indigne conculcamus. Si agnoscatur sufficiens, tum posita causa sufficienti in actu, nihil aliud requiritur ad effectum inducendum. Ex ipso igitur actu Christi seipsum Deo offerentis statim sequatur universalis liberatio omnium hominum a reatu peccatorum suorum, & universalis reconciliatio, sive receptio omnium hominum in gratiam Divinam.
